1Introduction

1.1What a test is here

Every test boots the real chip. The testbench loads a firmware image into ROM, releases reset, the chip powers itself up, and the Ibex CPU runs the image. A test then has up to two halves:

  • A firmware half — a C file that runs on the CPU, programs registers, and reports PASSED or FAILED.
  • A testbench half — a UVM test class that drives or watches pins, clocks or the bus, and adds its own checks.

A test can use either half or both. Independently of your code, every test also checks every bus transaction in the chip: 56 AXI monitors and the fabric scoreboard run all the time.

1.2Prerequisites

  • C for embedded systems (volatile, register access, interrupts)
  • SystemVerilog and the basics of UVM (tests, sequences, uvm_info)
  • Access to the simulation server with Cadence Xcelium

1.3Conventions

my_test stands for the name you choose. Paths are relative to the repository root. Shell commands are bash; csh users replace env.sh by env.csh.

2Before you start

2.1One-time setup

git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:auxeraglobaltech/amba-titan.git
cd amba-titan
~/.local/opt/python-3.11.15-titan/bin/python3 -m venv .venv      # project Python
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/accellera-official/uvm-core .tools/uvm-core   # for the lint check (optional)

2.2Every shell

# load your Cadence setup first (xrun on PATH), then:
source uvm/sim/env.sh            # RISC-V gcc, project Python; prints what it found

2.3Check the environment works

uvm/sim/run.sh fw_hello          # about 1 minute; expect:  RESULT: PASSED  fw_hello
CAUTIONRun one simulation at a time — the server and the build directory are shared. Before you change anything, run the regression (uvm/sim/regress.sh) so you know it was green when you started.

2.4Where files go

3Choosing the kind of test

Table 3-1. The four kinds of test

RecipeUse whenYou writetests.list line
A — C onlythe firmware can check everything itself (registers, interrupts, internal loopback)firmware/tests/my_test.cmy_test fw_test my_test
B — C + UVMthe testbench must drive or check pins, clocks or timing, or act at a precise point in the firmwarethe C file + a test classmy_test my_test_cls my_test
C — UVM onlybus-level tests: the testbench is the bus master (stub CPU); the CPU sleepsa sequence + a test classmy_test my_test_cls idle
D — TB onlythe testbench only observes the chip (clocks, pins after boot)a test classmy_test my_test_cls idle

4What happens when you run a test

Table 4-1. Pass criteria

KindThe test passes when
C, C + UVMthe firmware writes PASSED (main() returned 0), the UVM test's own checks raise no error, and no checker in the environment reports an error
UVM only, TB onlytest_body() finishes and no UVM error was reported (the firmware idle never reports PASSED)
Allthe log ends with *** TEST PASSED ***; run.sh prints RESULT: PASSED

Table 4-2. Time limits (in titan_base_test)

LimitValueMessage when exceeded
boot_timeout10 ms from POR to IN_TESTfirmware never reached main()
test_timeout20 ms from IN_TEST to the end of test_body()test body did not finish within ...

Override either in your test's constructor if a test legitimately needs longer (e.g. test_timeout = 40ms;).

5Recipe A — C-only test

EXAMPLECheck that delay_us(50) really waits 50 µs, measured with the hardware timer.
1

Write the C file

new file: firmware/tests/my_timer_test.c

// my_timer_test — C-only example: delay_us() really waits that long.
//
// Test entry (uvm/sim/tests.list):  my_timer_test   fw_test   my_timer_test

#include "titan.h"

int main(void) {
  timer_init_us();                         // rv_timer: 1 tick = 1 us
  uint64_t t0 = timer_now_us();
  delay_us(50);
  uint32_t dt = (uint32_t)(timer_now_us() - t0);

  titan_printf("my_timer_test: delay_us(50) took %u us\n", dt);
  CHECK(dt >= 50 && dt < 60, "delay_us(50) took %u us", dt);
  return 0;                                // 0 = PASSED
}
  • Include only titan.h (plus regs/<ip>_regs.h for direct register access).
  • Fail with CHECK(cond, fmt, ...): it prints file, line and your message, then reports FAILED.
  • Return 0 to pass. Do not loop forever: the test would end only at the timeout.
2

Check it compiles

make -C firmware TEST=my_timer_test      # → firmware/build/my_timer_test/my_timer_test.hex

Compiler warnings are errors (-Werror). The listing build/my_timer_test/my_timer_test.dis shows the code with source lines.

3

Register the test

edit: uvm/sim/tests.list — one line, three columns: name, UVM test class, firmware

my_timer_test       fw_test                 my_timer_test

fw_test is the generic UVM test for C-only tests: it waits for the firmware's PASSED/FAILED.

4

Run it

uvm/sim/run.sh my_timer_test

Expected lines in uvm/sim/runs/my_timer_test/run.log:

UVM_INFO ... uvm_test_top.env.sw [SW] firmware status: IN_TEST (main() started, boot 1)
UVM_INFO ... uvm_test_top.env.sw [SW] my_timer_test: delay_us(50) took 50 us
UVM_INFO ... uvm_test_top.env.sw [SW] firmware status: PASSED
UVM_INFO ... uvm_test_top.env.scoreboard [FABRIC_SB] ... transactions matched host->device, 0 DECERR, 0 errors, 0 resets
UVM_INFO ... uvm_test_top [TEST] *** TEST PASSED ***
5

Document it and commit

Add a section to uvm/TESTS.md and follow the checklist in §12.

6Recipe B — C + UVM test

EXAMPLEThe firmware makes a 10 µs pulse on GPIO0; the testbench measures its width at the pad.
1

Write the firmware half

new file: firmware/tests/my_gpio_pulse.c

// my_gpio_pulse — C + UVM example: firmware makes a 10 us pulse on GPIO0,
// the testbench measures it.
//
// Step 1 (titan_sync(1)): GPIO0 is an output, low; the pulse starts now.
// Step 2 (titan_sync(2)): the pulse is over.
// Keep the width in step with my_gpio_pulse_test (uvm/tests/titan_test_pkg.sv).
//
// Test entry:  my_gpio_pulse   my_gpio_pulse_test   my_gpio_pulse

#include "titan.h"

#define PULSE_US 10

int main(void) {
  timer_init_us();
  pinmux_connect_tb_gpios();               // GPIO[7:0] <-> pads IOB0..IOB7
  gpio_write(0);
  gpio_set_oe(0x1);                        // drive GPIO0 only

  titan_sync(1);
  gpio_write(1);
  delay_us(PULSE_US);
  gpio_write(0);
  titan_sync(2);
  return 0;
}
2

Write the testbench half

edit: uvm/tests/titan_test_pkg.sv — add the class inside the package, before endpackage

class my_gpio_pulse_test extends titan_base_test;
  `uvm_component_utils(my_gpio_pulse_test)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent);
    super.new(name, parent);
  endfunction

  virtual task test_body();
    realtime t_rise, t_fall;
    env.sw.wait_sync(1);                           // firmware: "pulse starts now"
    wait (env.gpio.vif.pins[0] === 1'b1);
    t_rise = $realtime;
    wait (env.gpio.vif.pins[0] === 1'b0);
    t_fall = $realtime;
    env.sw.wait_sync(2);                           // firmware: "pulse is over"
    if (t_fall - t_rise < 10us || t_fall - t_rise > 12us)
      `uvm_error("TEST", $sformatf("GPIO0 pulse was %0t, expected 10 us", t_fall - t_rise))
    else
      `uvm_info("TEST", $sformatf("GPIO0 pulse %0t", t_fall - t_rise), UVM_LOW)
    super.test_body();                             // wait for PASSED from the firmware
  endtask
endclass
  • `uvm_component_utils registers the class so +UVM_TESTNAME can find it — without it the run stops with "test not found".
  • test_body() starts after the firmware has written IN_TEST; the chip is booted and clocks are calibrated.
  • Call super.test_body() at the end so the test also waits for, and checks, the firmware's PASSED.
3

Register and run

# uvm/sim/tests.list
my_gpio_pulse       my_gpio_pulse_test      my_gpio_pulse

uvm/sim/run.sh my_gpio_pulse

6.1What the testbench can reach

Table 6-1. Environment handles available inside a test (env is a titan_env)

HandleUse
env.sw.wait_sync(n)block until the firmware calls titan_sync(n)
env.sw.ev_done, env.sw.passed(), env.sw.n_bootsfirmware finished / passed / how many times the chip booted
env.gpio.vif.pins[7:0]values on pads IOB0–IOB7 (GPIO[7:0])
env.gpio.vif.drv_en[i], env.gpio.vif.drv_val[i]drive pad IOBi from the testbench (a GPIO input to the chip)
env.gpio.valuesqueue of settled GPIO[7:0] values, in order
env.uart0.texteverything received from UART0 TX (1 Mbaud, 8N1)
env.uart0.vif.rxUART0 RX pin into the chip (idles high)
env.clk.count_edges(name, window, n), env.clk.measure_hz(name, window, hz)clocks: main io io_div2 io_div4 usb aon io_div4_peri io_div2_peri io_peri usb_peri
env.sim_master()sequencer of the testbench AXI master (Recipe C)

6.2Passing data between the halves

  • Firmware → testbench: titan_sync(n) for "step reached"; log text with titan_printf; pins.
  • Testbench → firmware: pins only (drive a GPIO input; the firmware polls it or takes an interrupt — see fw_plic_gpio_irq).
  • Shared constants (pattern tables, expected strings, timings) exist twice, in C and in SV. Nothing links them at compile time: put a comment on both sides naming the other file.

7Recipe C — UVM-only test (stub CPU)

EXAMPLEThe testbench writes 16 words to main SRAM over AXI and reads them back. The CPU runs the idle firmware and stays asleep.
1

Write the sequence and the test

edit: uvm/tests/titan_test_pkg.sv

class my_sram_pattern_seq extends axi_test_seq;
  `uvm_object_utils(my_sram_pattern_seq)
  function new(string name = "my_sram_pattern_seq");
    super.new(name);
  endfunction

  virtual task body();
    bit [31:0] base = 32'h1001_8000;               // above the firmware's data/stack
    bit [31:0] d;
    bit [1:0]  r;
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) begin
      write32(base + 4 * i, 32'hC0DE_0000 | i, r);
      check(r == AXI_OKAY, $sformatf("write %0d: %s", i, resp_name(r)));
    end
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) begin
      read32(base + 4 * i, d, r);
      check(r == AXI_OKAY && d == (32'hC0DE_0000 | i),
            $sformatf("word %0d = 0x%08h %s", i, d, resp_name(r)));
    end
  endtask
endclass

class my_sram_pattern_test extends axi_stub_cpu_test;
  `uvm_component_utils(my_sram_pattern_test)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent);
    super.new(name, parent);
  endfunction
  virtual function axi_test_seq make_seq();
    return my_sram_pattern_seq::type_id::create("my_sram_pattern_seq");
  endfunction
endclass
2

Register and run

# uvm/sim/tests.list — firmware is always 'idle' for UVM-only tests
my_sram_pattern     my_sram_pattern_test    idle

uvm/sim/run.sh my_sram_pattern

axi_stub_cpu_test runs your sequence on the testbench master and fails the test if the sequence's check() counted any error.

7.1Sequence helpers

Table 7-1. Provided by axi_base_seq / axi_test_seq

CallDoes
write32(addr, data, resp)single 32-bit write; resp = BRESP
read32(addr, data, resp)single 32-bit read
write(addr, data[$], strb[$], resp, len, size, burst, id)burst write (len = beats − 1; size 0/1/2; burst AXI_INCR/AXI_WRAP/AXI_FIXED; id < 16)
read(addr, data[$], resp[$], len, size, burst, id)burst read, one data and response per beat
check(ok, msg)count and report an error when ok is 0
resp_name(r); AXI_OKAY, AXI_SLVERR, AXI_DECERRresponses

7.2Rules for bus-level tests

  • Use main SRAM at 0x1001_0000 and above; the firmware's own data and stack occupy 0x1000_0000–0x1000_4FFF.
  • Expect DECERR for unmapped addresses, SLVERR for registers an IP refuses. The scoreboard checks routing for you either way.
  • Bursts are split into single accesses by the IP's bridge; registers usually want single 32-bit accesses.
  • Atomic operations (ATOPs) are answered SLVERR before the crossbar and never reach an IP.
  • Do not touch flash (0x2000_0000) or the retention SRAM before initializing them: an uninitialized flash read stalls, an uninitialized SRAM read returns X.

8Recipe D — testbench-only test

EXAMPLEMeasure the 24 MHz peripheral clock after boot.

edit: uvm/tests/titan_test_pkg.sv

class my_clk_check_test extends titan_base_test;
  `uvm_component_utils(my_clk_check_test)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent);
    super.new(name, parent);
  endfunction
  virtual task test_body();
    real hz;
    env.clk.measure_hz("io_div4", 20us, hz);
    if (hz < 23.5e6 || hz > 24.5e6)
      `uvm_error("TEST", $sformatf("clk_io_div4 = %.3f MHz, expected 24", hz / 1e6))
  endtask
endclass

// uvm/sim/tests.list
// my_clk_check        my_clk_check_test       idle

Do not call super.test_body() here: it would wait for a PASSED the idle firmware never writes, and the test would time out.

9Working with registers

Table 9-1. Where to find register information

You needFind it in
Base address of an IPC: TOP_EARLGREY_<IP>_BASE_ADDR in firmware/include/top_earlgrey.h; manual Table 4-1
Register offset and fieldsfirmware/include/regs/<ip>_regs.h: <IP>_<REG>_REG_OFFSET, _BIT, _MASK, _OFFSET
Reset values, field meaningthe IP's register description: vendor/opentitan/hw/ip/<ip>/data/<ip>.hjson (or hw/top_earlgrey/ip_autogen/<ip>/data/)
Interrupt ID of a peripheralkTopEarlgreyPlicIrqId<Ip><Irq> in top_earlgrey.h
Pinmux indiceskTopEarlgreyPinmuxPeripheralIn*, kTopEarlgreyPinmuxOutsel*, kTopEarlgreyPinmuxMioOut*, kTopEarlgreyPinmuxInsel*

C

#include "regs/uart_regs.h"
#include "titan.h"

uint32_t s = reg32_read(TOP_EARLGREY_UART0_BASE_ADDR,
                        UART_STATUS_REG_OFFSET);
CHECK(s & BIT(UART_STATUS_TXIDLE_BIT), "tx busy");

UVM sequence

// uart0 STATUS = 0x4000_0000 + 0x14
read32(32'h4000_0014, d, r);
check(r == AXI_OKAY && d == 32'h3C,
      $sformatf("STATUS = 0x%08h", d));
NOTEOut of reset the pinmux connects no pad. A firmware test that uses UART0 or GPIO pins must call pinmux_connect_uart0() or pinmux_connect_tb_gpios() first.

10Extending the environment

10.1A new firmware helper

  1. Add the function to firmware/lib/drivers.c (include the IP's regs/<ip>_regs.h there).
  2. Declare it in firmware/include/titan.h, in the drivers section.
  3. Rebuild all firmware (make -C firmware all) — every test links the library.

10.2An interrupt handler

Define titan_isr_external() (PLIC) or titan_isr_timer() in your test file; it overrides the default, which fails the test on any unexpected interrupt. Pattern for the PLIC: id = plic_claim() → clear the cause in the peripheral → plic_complete(id). Model: firmware/tests/plic_gpio_irq.c.

10.3A new pin-level agent (e.g. I2C, SPI)

  1. uvm/agents/<name>_agent/<name>_if.sv and <name>_agent_pkg.sv (model: uart_agent).
  2. Add both files to uvm/sim/uvm.f, interface before package.
  3. In uvm/tb/tb_top.sv: instantiate the interface, connect it to the pads (and remove those pads' pull-downs if you drive them), and put it into uvm_config_db.
  4. In uvm/env/titan_env_pkg.sv: import the package, add the component to titan_env, create it in build_phase.
  5. In firmware: route the peripheral to those pads with the pinmux.
  6. Lint (§11.3) before the first simulation.

11Running and debugging your test

11.1Commands

uvm/sim/run.sh my_test                       # run
uvm/sim/run.sh my_test --seed 7              # another seed
uvm/sim/run.sh my_test --waves               # waves: simvision uvm/sim/runs/my_test/waves.shm &
uvm/sim/run.sh my_test --trace 0x40000014    # every AXI port one address crossed
uvm/sim/run.sh my_test --verbosity UVM_HIGH  # every AXI transaction on every port
uvm/sim/run.sh my_test --print               # show the commands only

11.2Reading the log

Table 11-1. Log tags

TagSource
[TB]testbench top: which images were loaded
[SW]the firmware: its status, its log text, sync steps (at UVM_MEDIUM)
[TEST], [SEQ]your UVM test and sequences
[FABRIC_SB]interconnect scoreboard: summary at the end, or an error
[uart0], [TRACE]UART monitor lines; address trace

11.3Compile check without a simulator

uvm/sim/lint.py --top tb_top --uvm -D TITAN_SIM -D SIMULATION rtl/flist/rtl.f uvm/sim/uvm.f

Finds syntax, type and port errors in about a minute. Run it after every SystemVerilog change.

11.4Common problems

Table 11-2. Problems when adding a test

SymptomCause and fix
test 'my_test' not in uvm/sim/tests.listadd the line (name, class, firmware)
UVM_FATAL ... Requested test ... not foundthe class is missing `uvm_component_utils, or is outside titan_test_pkg, or its name differs from tests.list
make: ... No rule to make target 'tests/x.c'the firmware column of tests.list does not match a file in firmware/tests/
BUILD FAILEDrun the lint; then uvm/sim/runs/build/build.log
test body did not finishusually a wait_sync(n) for a step the firmware never reaches (wrong number, or the firmware failed first: look for [SW] CHECK FAILED above)
UVM-only test times outsuper.test_body() called with idle firmware
[SW] EXCEPTION mcause=5/7 mtval=...load/store to an address no device owns (DECERR); mtval is the address
[SW] unexpected ... interruptan interrupt is enabled but the test has no handler
pins never changepinmux not connected, or output enable not set
the firmware change has no effectyou edited a different firmware than the one named in tests.list
FABRIC_SB errorsa real interconnect problem, or a transaction to a gated / uninitialized IP — see the manual §9

12Before you commit

  • The test passes: uvm/sim/run.sh my_test, and with a second seed
  • It really checks something: temporarily break the expectation and see it fail
  • Shared constants are commented on both sides (C and SV)
  • The line is in uvm/sim/tests.list (only once it passes)
  • A section in uvm/TESTS.md: goal, method, pass criteria
  • The full regression is green: uvm/sim/regress.sh
  • The documents are regenerated: .venv/bin/python uvm/doc/gen_guide.py (updates both HTML files' test lists)
  • Only firmware/, uvm/ and the generated HTML changed: git status
git checkout -b test/my_test                       # or work on main if that is the team's rule
git add firmware/tests/my_test.c uvm/tests/titan_test_pkg.sv uvm/sim/tests.list uvm/TESTS.md *.html
git commit -m "Add my_test: <what it verifies>"
git push -u origin test/my_test
